name: Barbell Hip Thrust
summary: A glute-focused lift where the upper back is supported on a bench and you drive a loaded barbell upward with your hips. It lets you load the glutes heavily in the shortened position.
setup: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the side of a stable bench and roll the bar over your legs to your hips, using a pad if needed.
Place your feet about hip width apart, shins about vertical at the top, and the bench edge just below your shoulder blades.
Hold the bar steady with both hands.
Tuck your chin slightly and brace your trunk.
execution: Drive through your feet and lift your hips until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glutes at the top with your shins close to vertical.
Keep your ribs down and chin tucked so you do not overarch your lower back.
Lower your hips under control until the bar is near the floor, without resting.
Repeat, then roll the bar off when finished.
cues: Squeeze the glutes at the top
mistakes: Overarching the lower back at the top: tuck the ribs down and stop when the hips and torso are in line.
Feet too far forward or too close: adjust so your shins are about vertical at lockout.
Pushing through the toes: keep the whole foot, especially the heel, planted.
Bar rolling or hurting the hips: use a thick pad and keep the bar centered.
